column15: Verified via Wikipedia (Powers (whiskey)), fetched this session: Irish Distillers/Pernod Ricard-owned, produced at Midleton; John's Lane Release is a 12yo single pot still expression (matured mainly in ex-bourbon casks with some sherry-cask input), a relaunch of the pre-1976 single-pot-still style, distinct from the standard Powers Gold Label blend. No peat mentioned; Irish pot still whiskey is never peated. Confidence raised from low to high.

Identified this session (seed round found no web presence): Prologue is independent bottler Chapter 7 Whisky's blended-malt series, vatted from Speyside+Highland single malts in bourbon casks, ~6000-bottle batches, no age statement. New bottlerSlug row chapter-7 created (see below). Standard batches are unpeated per scotchnoob.com's review (no peat mentioned); "Prologue Peated" is a distinct small-batch edition confirmed directly on chapter7whisky.com's own site (Prologue Peated Edition 4, World Edition 2/3, IWCS Silver 90pts) - handled as a name-pattern rule rather than a separate row, per the Bruichladdich/Port Charlotte precedent - see rule.tsv.

Louisville, KY distillery; confirmed via official site (fetched this session), whose footer links to pernod-ricard.com confirm Pernod Ricard ownership. Core Four line (Cavehill, Heigold, Dareringer, Boxergrail) spans bourbon and a 95%-rye whiskey, so defaultTypeName is left empty. Mash bills (corn/wheat/barley/rye combinations) confirmed to contain no peated malt; no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere on the official site. Confidence raised from low to high.

Northern California craft whiskey producer; official products page (fetched this session) confirms the full range spans bourbon (Pipe Dream, Colonel Armstrong, Screaming Titan, Grizzly Beast), rye (Emerald Giant, Van Duzen, Rocket Top, Devils Tower), a blend (Lost Monarch, Hyperion) and a single malt (Foggy Burl) - defaultTypeName correctly left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere on the page. Confidence raised from low to high.

Identified this session (seed round exhausted its search budget with no match). "River Proof Series" is a distillery-exclusive bourbon line from Augusta Distillery (Augusta, Kentucky area; founded by Lance Bates and partners), sold via Kentucky Bourbon Direct (wheated bourbon) and CaskCartel (straight bourbon, 61.6% ABV). Both retailer pages were fetched directly this session; no official Augusta Distillery site could be located. Reclassified kind from blend to brand (a single distillery's exclusive line, not a blended product) and countryCode from XX to US. No peat mentioned; US bourbon mash bills are not peated.

Catalogue brand string for this row is "Seagram's Gin" but the sample product is "Seagram's Royal Stag Deluxe" - an Indian whisky (blend of Indian grain spirits + imported Scotch malts, launched 1995, Pernod Ricard-owned since 2001), not a gin; almost certainly a shop miscategorisation - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW of the "Seagram's Gin" catalogue string. Confirmed via Wikipedia and Pernod Ricard's own brand page (both fetched this session). No source states peat use; treated as an ordinary mass-market blend (no smoky/peaty marketing, only a generic "touch of smoke" tasting note). Confidence raised from low to high.

Retried this session (Total Wine, CraftShack, WoodenCork, HiProof, DramFellows product pages checked directly): confirms "RY3 Cigar Series Cask Strength" is a real 60.6% ABV rye whiskey with rum/Madeira/naranja cask finishing, but no page names the actual distiller, producer, state or country - likely an NDP (non-distiller-producer) sourced-whiskey label. No Wikipedia page and no official site could be found. Country and category remain undetermined; kept at low confidence per the brief ("world is genuinely silent").

Models "Seagram's V.O." Canadian whisky, produced at the Valleyfield distillery (Quebec); confirmed directly on Sazerac's own brand page (fetched this session) as "Canadian Whisky" under Sazerac Brands, sold to Sazerac by Diageo in 2018 following the 2000 break-up of the original Seagram company. Blend of separately-aged corn/barley/rye whiskies, min. 6 years. The sample "100 Pipers 1970's (Seagram's)" is a different, Pernod-Ricard-India-owned Scotch blend that merely carries the historical Seagram name in some listings; not modeled by this row. No peat mentioned; Canadian whisky mash bills are not peated. Confidence raised from low to high.

Secret Orkney/"Undisclosed Orkney" is a generic descriptor used by many different independent bottlers (Signatory Vintage, Douglas Laing, Brühler Whiskyhaus, The Single Cask Ltd, Malt Grain & Cane, etc.) for undisclosed-source single malt from Orkney. Reclassified kind from blend to brand and added defaultTypeName=single malt, since it is never a blended product - confirmed via two independent review/reference sites fetched this session. Multiple sources agree it is "pretty much always" Highland Park, since Scapa does not release independent bottlings (Orkney has only these two distilleries) - deliberately not asserted as parentSlug since no single label discloses it. withheld peat proposal: light, per moredramslessdrama.com's tasting notes across three Secret Orkney bottlings ("delicate smoke", "faint ethereal smoke", "smoked oranges"), consistent with Highland Park's typical light peat - kept unknown since the source distillery is deliberately undisclosed by design on every release of this label, so no producer-domain confirmation is possible.

Catalogue brand string is "Whisky of Voodoo" but every sampled product actually reads "Spirit of Voodoo ..." - modelled under the real product-line name, both spellings aliased - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW of the "Whisky of Voodoo" catalogue string. Identified this session (seed round's search budget was exhausted): Spirit of Voodoo is a range from Brave New Spirits, a Glasgow-based independent bottler/blender (new bottlerSlug row created, see below) - corrected countryCode from XX to GB-SCT and kind from blend to brand. Blood Moon (13yo) is single grain Scotch from North British Distillery (Lowland), confirmed via CaskCartel's product page fetched this session; Mask of Death (10yo) is Speyside single malt and The Dancing Cultist (12yo) undisclosed Highland single malt per Master of Malt - spans grain+malt across three regions, so region/legalRegion/defaultTypeName are left empty. No peat stated for any of the three; kept unknown.

Dewar Rattray's own recreated blended-malt brand, named after a long-closed distillery not present in the Wikipedia operating-distilleries authority file. Retried this session: whisky.com's company profile page returned 403 and dewarrattray.com failed on a DNS/certificate mismatch, so no further citation could be opened; kept at low confidence, unchanged from the seed round.

No web presence found (Wikipedia, DuckDuckGo and Bing searches empty or blocked this session too). All 3 samples are just "Charles House" with no other descriptor. Corrected peatProfile from none to unknown: the seed round's "none" assumed an ordinary blended Scotch, but country/identity were never actually verified, so the brief's category-default reasoning for "ordinary blended Scotch" does not apply here. Dropped the generic en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blended_whiskey citation since it does not verify this specific brand's existence.

Confirmed by direct fetch this session: created 1882 in Leith by William Sanderson & Son, Diageo-owned since the Distillers Company absorbed Sanderson in 1937; a blend of about 40 malt and grain whiskies (explicitly "not a vatted malt" despite the name). No peat mentioned. Confidence raised from low to high.

Seattle, WA American single malt distillery. Corrected owner from empty to Rémy Cointreau, confirmed via Wikipedia (fetched this session). Official site's current core range (Flagship, Garryana, Solum, Colere, cask finishes) states no peat; a customer review on the Flagship page speculating "peaty smoke" is not an official claim and was disregarded. This batch's own samples include "Westland Peated" - captured as a rule (see rule.tsv) from the product's own name, but no current westlanddistillery.com page for that specific release could be located this session (it is absent from the current homepage lineup, and guessed product URLs 404'd) - withheld peat proposal: heavy (unconfirmed intensity), same caveat as the seed round.

Vermont rye whiskey producer (Shoreham). Confirmed spelling "WhistlePig" (catalogue spells it "Whistlepig") via the official site fetched this session, which confirms the rye-only focus (PiggyBack, Small Batch, FarmStock) and states no peat anywhere. Dropped the unrelated en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_whiskey citation from the seed round (stray/irrelevant). peatProfile=none via the general "American rye mash bills are not peated" category fact, now additionally supported by the official site's silence on the topic. Confidence raised from low to high.

No web presence found this session either; country and style could not be identified. This session's web-search budget ran out before a dedicated search for this row could be issued, and retailer-aggregator fallbacks (wine-searcher, Bing, DuckDuckGo) were blocked (403/CAPTCHA) for every attempt made across this batch's obscure own-label rows. Kept unchanged from the seed round.

Samples (Yuzu, Classic, Passion Fruit) read as a flavoured whisky-based drink rather than a conventional Scotch/Japanese whisky - possibly a liqueur/RTD rather than whisky, but no source could be opened this session to confirm either way (zero search hits, retailer-aggregator lookups blocked), so kept in producer.tsv rather than rejected without evidence, per the brief's "cite evidence for the verdict, when in doubt keep it low" rule. FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW (possible fruit liqueur, not whisky). Likely a fantasy/evocative brand name for the Eastern European market rather than an actual Japanese producer - left fully unknown rather than assume Japan from the name alone.

No web presence found. Re-attempted this session; the web-search budget ran out partway through the batch and retailer/search-engine fallbacks (wine-searcher, Bing, DuckDuckGo) were all blocked. Naming pattern ("Platinum", "First West") gives no clear nationality signal, so left unclassified rather than guessed.

North Wales single malt distillery (first in North Wales since the early 1900s), Station Road, Abergwyngregyn. Re-fetched the official site directly this session: confirms Halewood Artisanal Spirits PLC ownership and the single malt focus; still no peat/smoke mention anywhere on the site. Confidence raised from low to high given this session's direct re-verification of every asserted field.

Could not identify producer despite renewed research this session (web-search budget exhausted, retailer-aggregator fallbacks blocked). Only sample is "Alexander Aqva Di Vita Amarone Cask Finish" - the stylised "Aqva Di Vita" spelling (Latin for "water of life", the etymological root of whisky/aquavit) plus an Amarone (Italian wine) cask finish both point toward a small Italian or generic European craft producer, but this remains a naming-pattern guess, not an asserted fact. FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW.

Louisville, Kentucky distillery (Louisville Distilling Co LLC), known for port-cask-finished bourbon. Corrected defaultTypeName from bourbon to empty: the official site (fetched this session) confirms a rye whiskey (finished in Caribbean rum casks) alongside the bourbon range, so not every bottling is bourbon. Bacardi Limited ownership (acquired 2015) now directly confirmed via the official site's own footer/brand-partnership references, replacing the seed round's unconfirmed general-knowledge claim. No peat mentioned anywhere. Confidence raised from low to high.

No information found. The seed round explicitly did not search this one ("long tail budget"), and this session's own search attempt hit the web-search budget cap before returning a result. Samples are "Back to Black" / "The Story of Back to Black" - own-label, origin unclear. Genuinely unverified rather than guessed.

Formerly Connacht Distillery (Co. Mayo, est. 2015), rebranded Ballina in 2025 after acquisition by Terroirs Distillers (also Tullibardine's owner). Directly re-fetched the Irish Whiskey Magazine article this session, confirming the ownership, Co. Mayo/River Moy location and the two debut expressions (Dubailte Double Wood, Triarach Triple Wood), both 100% Irish malted barley. No peat mentioned in either source. Confidence raised from low to high given this session's direct re-verification.

new row for prologue. Independent bottler founded 2014 by Selim Evin (inspired by his Scottish grandfather); opened its own bottling facility in Glasgow in 2022, relocated to Burnobennie Distillery, Banchory (Scottish Highlands) in October 2025. Multiple ranges (Monologue, Anecdote, Chronicle, Prologue, Simple Malt, Rebel, Four Angels, Peat Legends) span both peated and unpeated whisky from many distilleries/regions, so no producer-level peat or type default applies.

new row for spirit-of-voodoo. Glasgow-based independent bottler and blender of Scotch whisky (single malts, single grain and blends), releasing the "Spirit of Voodoo" range among others. Spans multiple distilleries/regions with no single peat or type default.
